title: Spring constant calculation
description: Essential Criteria: The response must correctly calculate the spring constant as k = 2mg/L from the equilibrium condition mg = k(0.5L).

title: Configuration A analysis
description: Important Criteria: The response must correctly determine the elongation of each spring in configuration A, showing the top spring elongates by L and the bottom by 0.5L.

title: Configuration B analysis
description: Important Criteria: The response must correctly determine the total elongation in configuration B as 2L, recognizing the series connection and equal force.

title: Total length comparison
description: Essential Criteria: The response must state the final total lengths (3.5L for A, 4L for B) and correctly identify which is longer.

title: Force equilibrium reasoning
description: Important Criteria: The response must apply Newton's First Law to set spring force equal to the weight(s) supported for each spring in both configurations.

title: Unit consistency
description: Optional Criteria: The response should maintain consistent units throughout the calculation or explicitly note the spring constant units.

title: Misidentifying spring force
description: Pitfall Criteria: Penalize if the student incorrectly assumes the force in a spring is the same for all springs in a series-parallel configuration without proper force analysis.

title: Arithmetic or algebraic error
description: Pitfall Criteria: Penalize for simple arithmetic mistakes in calculating elongations or total lengths, such as incorrectly summing L + x.
